summary.headline: Epack Prefab H1 FY27 revenue rose 19% to INR 867 crore and Q2 hit a record INR 501 crore, but margins and working capital slipped.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue grew 19% to INR 867 crore, with Q2 the company's largest quarter at INR 501 crore. Profit grew only 2% and operating cash flow was negative, as steel and input cost inflation outran pass-through on existing orders and gross margin fell about 2.3%. Working capital rose to nearly 60 days against a 40-55 day guidance band, driven by LC-backed milestone receivables (up about INR 144 crore) and deliberate steel inventory build (about INR 92 crore). Management maintained FY27 guidance of INR 1,900 crore revenue and 10-10.5% EBITDA margin, and said Q2 margin recovered to 10.1% from 9.4% in Q1.

financial_highlights.change: Due to steel and input cost increases
Stated as about INR 1,420 crore in a later answer

segments.name: PEB (pre-engineered buildings)
segments.commentary: Average order value expected at INR 10-12 crore this year; run rate close to INR 150 crore per quarter cited for prefab execution. Largest single order of about INR 155 crore was 95% built, with handover delayed to December end by customer civil works.

segments.name: Sandwich panels
segments.commentary: Mambattu (Andhra Pradesh) utilisation rose from about 35% in Q1 to 47-48% in Q2; pending sandwich panel order book above 5 lakh sq m. New Ghiloth (Rajasthan) sandwich panel line commissioned in late October 2026 for the northern market.

segments.name: Structural steel / data centre
segments.commentary: First structural steel supply order for a data centre expected in Q3; handled within existing lines (up to 2 m web width, typically up to 25 mm). A separate data-centre subsidiary floated last quarter is still at discussion stage with one large customer.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR 1,900 crore (one answer cited INR 1,900-1,950 crore), with EBITDA margin of 10-10.5%.
Management expects Q3 and H2 margins to be better than H1, with H2 better in both revenue and margin; new orders priced on current input costs.
Working capital expected to normalise in Q3 as LC-backed milestone receivables are collected; management will report working capital every quarter until normalised.
Revenue CAGR of 25-30% targeted for the next couple of years; FY27-FY28 expected to need no new capex, with 80-85% utilisation targeted on new plants.
Gujarat greenfield plant (first phase 50,000 tonnes of an 80,000+ tonne design) to commence manufacturing in Q4 FY27; capacity of 2,800-3,000 crore revenue cited with Gujarat and Ghiloth in place.
capex_capacity: Ghiloth Unit 5 (Greenfield): 13,000 tonnes of steel processing capacity added on 30 October 2026; sandwich panel line commissioned in Ghiloth, Rajasthan.
Gujarat greenfield plant: two lines to start, design capacity of four-five lines (about 80,000 tonnes); first phase 50,000 tonnes, commissioning targeted in Q4 FY27.
Mambattu (Andhra Pradesh) greenfield structural steel expansion completed after the IPO; one line added there, per management.
Ghiloth sandwich panel ramp-up expected over the next 5 months of FY27; management expects it to be stronger than the South ramp-up.
Peak revenue potential at current plus pending capacity: about INR 2,800-3,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Order inflow H1 FY27 INR 1,124 crore (+71% YoY) against an internal FY27 target of INR 2,000 crore.
Order book INR 1,462 crore, giving revenue visibility of 8-9 months; management said roughly 150 crore per quarter run rate.
Steel exposure about 48-50% hedged for the next 3-4 months; new orders priced at current input costs; price-increase requests to customers on existing large orders, with some accepted.
Raw material prices up 17-18% in Q2 per management, yet margin still improved from Q1; HR steel cited at about INR 70,000/tonne, which management sees as a peak.

Top five customers 28-30% of the order book; about 70% of revenue from new orders and 60% of order book from new customers over 3-4 years; more than 100 new customers added in H1 (20-30 in sandwich panels cold storage, 40-50 generic).
Management sees no capex deferment from customers due to price increases; building cost is a small share of total project capex. Pipeline cited in logistics, warehousing, automotive and data centres.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term growth guidance for FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 25-30% CAGR and said it expects to grow 25%+ YoY for the next couple of years, with capacity and team in place.

qa_highlights.question: Were steel price increases passed through on ongoing orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, price increases were obtained on existing orders, which helped Q2 margin recover to 10.1% from 9.4% despite raw material up 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: How much capacity is available for data centre heavy structures?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing lines handle up to 2 m web width, with data centre webs typically up to 25 mm, so no additional capex is needed for now. Management will not offer full turnkey semiconductor solutions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of NCR GRAP curbs?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply continues as customers gave go-ahead; execution may be disrupted post-Diwali when GRAP applies, but PEB construction can continue if customer civil work is ready.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company hedge steel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: About 48-50% of steel exposure covered, pending order book covers 3-4 months, new orders priced at current rates, and price increases sought from customers on large orders.

qa_highlights.question: Is there customer concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest order was about 10% of last year's revenue; top five customers 28-30% of order book; management says concentration is low.

qa_highlights.question: Will customer self-manufacturing be a competitive threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not aware of any client setting up its own PEB facility, so it could not comment.

risks_watch: Working capital at nearly 60 days versus 40-55 day guidance; LC-backed receivables of about INR 144 crore must normalise in Q3.
Gross margin down about 2.3%; H2 margin recovery depends on pricing new orders at current input costs and on customer price escalation clauses, which management said are not yet standard practice.
Negative operating cash flow in H1 FY27 despite profit growth.
Delay in handover of the INR 155 crore order to December end because of customer civil-work delays.
NCR GRAP curbs may disrupt execution after Diwali; Gujarat plant commissioning in Q4 FY27 must hold; data centre subsidiary timing uncertain.
Management's H1 order book figure differs between answers (INR 1,462 crore vs about INR 1,420 crore), which should be reconciled.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, capacity and order book, but openly cautious on margin and cash: management acknowledged slippage in working capital and gross margin, and was less specific on timing of data centre and semiconductor opportunities. Some answers were hedged, for example on customer escalation clauses and the subsidiary timeline.
key_quotes: The profit grew by 2%, but the operating cash flow was negative.
H1 has shown that the demand is real, and H2 is all about showing you that we can convert it into margin and cash.
So, every new order is now priced on current input cost, and we have long -term sourcing arrangements in place.

adds.what: Ghiloth Unit 5 greenfield: 13,000 tonnes steel processing capacity plus sandwich panel line (Rajasthan)
Gujarat greenfield plant, first phase 50,000 tonnes of 80,000+ tonne design
Mambattu (Andhra Pradesh) greenfield structural steel expansion, one line added post-IPO

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR 1,900 crore (maintained, one answer said 1,900-1,950), with H2 better than H1 and a 25-30% CAGR targeted; backing is partly specific (Gujarat first phase 50,000 t in Q4 FY27, Ghiloth line live, INR 1,124 cr H1 order inflow and INR 1,462 cr order book) but Gujarat timing and the 25-30% CAGR are not fully evidenced.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin recovered to 10.1% from 9.4% in Q1 after steel pass-through, management expects H2 margin better than H1, and FY27 guided at 10-10.5%, though gross margin fell about 2.3% and raw material rose 17-18%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gujarat greenfield first phase of 50,000 tonnes is under construction with commissioning targeted in Q4 FY27, and Ghiloth Unit 5 (13,000 t plus sandwich panel line) was commissioned on 30 Oct 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 order inflow of INR 1,124 crore (+71% YoY) and order book of INR 1,462 crore give 8-9 months visibility, with Mambattu sandwich utilisation rising from about 35% to 47-48% and H2 guided above H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said no new capex is needed in FY27-FY28, with Gujarat and Ghiloth in place and 80-85% utilisation targeted on new plants; utilisation is only about 47.5% at Mambattu, so near-term announcement is unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,900 crore was only maintained (one answer cited 1,900-1,950 crore) and the EBITDA margin band of 10-10.5% was held, not raised, despite H1 revenue of INR 867 crore (+19%).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Working capital at nearly 60 days versus a 40-55 day band, negative operating cash flow, and H2 margin recovery depends on pricing new orders at current input costs and customer price escalation clauses that are not yet standard.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First structural steel supply order for a data centre is expected in Q3 within existing lines, but the separate data-centre subsidiary is still at discussion stage with one customer and timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Gujarat and data-centre order flow
rows.why: Order inflow of INR 1,124 crore in H1 against an internal FY27 target of INR 2,000 crore implies about INR 876 crore needed in H2, and a first data-centre order is expected in Q3.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation
rows.why: Working capital at nearly 60 days (up 15-18 days) is expected to normalise as about INR 144 crore of LC-backed milestone receivables are collected, with quarterly reporting until normal.

rows.label: NCR GRAP curbs disrupt execution
rows.why: Execution may be disrupted post-Diwali under GRAP, and the INR 155 crore PEB order handover is already delayed to December end due to customer civil works.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, order book and capacity, but cautious on gross margin, working capital and negative operating cash flow, and hedged on customer escalation clauses and the data-centre subsidiary timeline; the brief does not record analyst questions in detail, so analysts are rated
